title: Japan Names 26-Man World Cup Squad — Mitoma Out With Hamstring, Tomiyasu Returns After Two-Year Absence
detail: Coach Hajime Moriyasu announced Japan's final 26-man World Cup squad in Tokyo on May 15, with Brighton winger Kaoru Mitoma the most prominent omission — ruled out after sustaining a hamstring injury in a Premier League fixture against Wolves. Moriyasu called Mitoma's absence 'a huge blow.' Arsenal/Ajax defender Takehiro Tomiyasu makes a remarkable return to the Samurai Blue after nearly two years away from international football due to injury. Veteran left back Yuto Nagatomo is selected for a record-equalling fifth World Cup appearance — one of the landmark individual milestones of the 2026 tournament. The 26-man squad features six Bundesliga players. Full squad includes GK: Zion Suzuki, Keisuke Osako, Tomoki Hayakawa; DEF: Nagatomo, Shogo Taniguchi, Ko Itakura, Tsuyoshi Watanabe, Tomiyasu, Hiroki Ito, Ayumu Seko, Yukinari Sugawara, Junnosuke Suzuki; MID: Wataru Endo, Junya Ito, Daichi Kamada, Ritsu Doan, Ao Tanaka, Kaishu Sano, Takefusa Kubo, Yuito Suzuki; FWD: Daizen Maeda, Koki Ogawa, Ayase Ueda, Keito Nakamura, Kento Shiogai, Keisuke Goto. Japan are in Group F: opening vs the Netherlands on June 14 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, then Tunisia (June 21, Guadalajara), Sweden (June 25, Arlington).

media.caption: Japan coach Moriyasu announces 26-man World Cup squad May 15 — Mitoma out with hamstring injury; Tomiyasu returns after 2-year absence; Nagatomo selected for fifth World Cup

title: Belgium Announces 26-Man World Cup Squad — Romeo Lavia Among Notable Absentees
detail: Belgium announced its final 26-man World Cup squad on May 15 under coach Domenico Tedesco. Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia was among the notable absentees from the Red Devils' selection. Belgium are drawn in Group G alongside Iran, New Zealand, and Egypt — they face Iran on June 21 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles in one of the tournament's most politically charged group-stage fixtures given the active US-Iran conflict. Multiple other nations also announced their final squads on May 15, including Tunisia, Ivory Coast, and Haiti, as the global squad announcement window reached its peak ahead of FIFA's full publication of all 48 squads on June 2.
